items.title: Types of Schemes & the DBT/JAM Delivery Backbone
items.body:
### How government schemes are classified and delivered

**In one line**
Government schemes come in two funding types — Central Sector (fully Union-funded) and Centrally Sponsored (cost shared with states) — and most now pay beneficiaries directly through DBT, which rides on the JAM trinity.

**Why it is asked**
The exam tests which scheme is which type (PM-KISAN vs MGNREGA), the typical cost-sharing ratios, and the full form and purpose of DBT and JAM.

**The story (cause → what happened → result)**
Because many welfare subjects (health, housing, water) are **State List** matters, the Centre cannot simply run them alone, so it created **Centrally Sponsored Schemes** where the Centre and states share the cost. Where the subject is national, the Centre runs a **Central Sector Scheme** and pays 100%. For decades, benefits leaked through middlemen and 'ghost' beneficiaries, so the government built **Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)** to pay people straight into their bank accounts — made possible by the **JAM trinity**.

**Picture it (two scheme types)**

| Feature | Central Sector Scheme | Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) |
|---|---|---|
| Funding | 100% by the Union | Shared Centre–State (e.g. 60:40; 90:10 for special-category) |
| Subject | Central List / national scope | Largely State List subjects |
| Examples | PM-KISAN, PM Suryaghar | MGNREGA, PMAY, Jal Jeevan Mission, POSHAN |

**Terms explained**
- **Central Sector Scheme** — fully funded and run by the Union government.
- **Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS)** — cost shared between Centre and states, usually on a fixed ratio.
- **DBT (Direct Benefit Transfer)** — paying a subsidy or benefit straight into the beneficiary's bank account.
- **JAM trinity** — **J**an Dhan (bank accounts) + **A**adhaar (unique ID) + **M**obile (connectivity): the digital rails that make DBT work.

**Don't confuse**
- **PM-KISAN** is a **Central Sector** scheme (100% Union), while **MGNREGA/PMAY** are **Centrally Sponsored** (shared cost) — a common trap.
- Special-category and north-eastern/hill states usually get a **more favourable ratio (e.g. 90:10)**, not the standard 60:40.

**Remember it**
'**Central Sector = Centre's full bill; CSS = shared bill**'; DBT runs on **JAM**.

**TL;DR**
- Central Sector Schemes are 100% Union-funded (e.g. PM-KISAN); CSS share cost Centre–State (e.g. MGNREGA, PMAY, Jal Jeevan Mission).
- DBT transfers benefits directly to bank accounts, reducing leakage and middlemen.
- JAM trinity = Jan Dhan + Aadhaar + Mobile — the digital backbone of DBT.
- Special-category/NE and hill states often get a 90:10 CSS ratio.

DBT transfers benefits directly to bank accounts, reducing leakage and middlemen.

items.title: Major Central Welfare Schemes — Quick Table
items.body:
### The flagship central welfare schemes

**In one line**
These are the Union government's big-ticket welfare schemes — income support, health cover, housing, jobs, cooking gas and water — each with a core benefit the exam asks you to recall.

**Why it is asked**
Prelims routinely asks the exact benefit (₹6,000, ₹5 lakh, 100 days) or the ministry behind a named scheme.

**The story (why these exist)**
To reduce poverty and deliver basic needs, the Centre runs a cluster of schemes that each target one gap: PM-KISAN for farmer income, Ayushman Bharat for hospital bills, PMAY for a pucca house, MGNREGA for guaranteed rural work, Ujjwala for clean cooking fuel, and Jal Jeevan Mission for tap water. Together they form India's modern welfare architecture.

**Picture it (scheme → domain → benefit)**

| Scheme | Ministry / Domain | Core benefit |
|---|---|---|
| PM-KISAN | Agriculture | ₹6,000/yr income support (3 × ₹2,000) |
| Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY | Health (NHA) | ₹5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary hospitalisation; all citizens 70+ covered irrespective of income (2024) |
| PMAY (Urban 2.0 / Gramin) | Housing | Pucca houses with basic amenities — 'Housing for All' |
| MGNREGA (2005) | Rural Development | Guaranteed at least 100 days of wage employment a year to a rural household whose adults volunteer for unskilled manual work — replaced from 1 July 2026 by the VB-G RAM G Act, 2025 (125 days) |
| PM Ujjwala Yojana | Petroleum | Free LPG connections to women of poor/BPL households |
| Jal Jeevan Mission | Jal Shakti | 'Har Ghar Jal' tap connections |
| PMJDY | Finance | Financial inclusion through basic zero-balance bank accounts |
| PM SVANidhi / PM Vishwakarma | Urban / MSME | Micro-credit to vendors; artisan support |
| PM Suryaghar Muft Bijli | New & Renewable Energy | Rooftop solar, up to 300 units of free electricity per month |

**Terms explained**
- **PM-JAY** — Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana, the health-insurance arm of Ayushman Bharat (₹5 lakh/family/year).
- **Pucca house** — a permanent house of durable material (as opposed to a kachha/temporary hut).
- **POSHAN Abhiyaan / POSHAN 2.0** — the national mission against malnutrition, stunting and anaemia.
- **NEP 2020** — the National Education Policy, introducing the 5+3+3+4 school structure and mother-tongue early learning.

**Don't confuse**
- **PM-KISAN** (cash to farmers) vs **PM-JAY** (health cover) vs **PMAY** (housing) — similar prefixes, different domains.
- Ayushman Bharat's **70+ universal cover** was added in **2024** — it now covers all senior citizens aged 70 and above regardless of income.

**Remember it**
Central big-ticket chain: '**KISAN–AYUSHMAN–AWAS–NAREGA–UJJWALA–JAL**' = income, health, house, work, gas, water.

**TL;DR**
- PM-KISAN = ₹6,000/year in three instalments (central sector).
- Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY = ₹5 lakh family health cover; extended to all 70+ in 2024.
- MGNREGA (2005) guaranteed 100 days of wage employment with social audit; the VB-G RAM G Act 2025 (125 days) replaced it from 1 July 2026.
- PM Ujjwala = free LPG to poor women; Jal Jeevan Mission = 'Har Ghar Jal' tap water.
- PM Suryaghar Muft Bijli Yojana (2024) subsidises rooftop solar with up to 300 free units.
keyPoints: PM-KISAN = ₹6,000/year in three installments (central sector).
Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY = ₹5 lakh family health cover; extended to all 70+ in 2024.
MGNREGA (2005) guaranteed 100 days of wage employment with social audit; the VB-G RAM G Act 2025 (125 days) replaced it from 1 July 2026.
PM Ujjwala = free LPG to poor women; Jal Jeevan Mission = 'Har Ghar Jal' tap water.
PM Suryaghar Muft Bijli Yojana (2024) subsidises rooftop solar with up to 300 free units.

items.title: AP Flagship — The 'Super Six' Guarantees (2024 TDP-NDA)
items.body:
### Andhra Pradesh's 'Super Six' guarantees

**In one line**
The 'Super Six' are the six headline welfare guarantees of the TDP-led NDA government that took office in Andhra Pradesh in June 2024, each a direct cash or in-kind benefit to a target group.

**Why it is asked**
As a state-current-affairs favourite for APPSC, the exam tests the names, target groups and amounts of the Super Six, and whether you can tell them apart from the previous YSRCP 'Navaratnalu'.

**The story (cause → what happened → result)**
In the 2024 Assembly election the alliance of **TDP, Jana Sena and BJP** promised six flagship guarantees to win power; it formed the government under CM **N. Chandrababu Naidu** in **June 2024** and began rolling the six out in phases over 2024–2026. The package was branded the **'Super Six'**.

**Picture it (the six guarantees)**

| # | Scheme | Core benefit |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Thalliki Vandanam | ~₹15,000/yr per child to mothers for schooling |
| 2 | Annadata Sukhibhava | ~₹20,000/yr to farmer families (incl. PM-KISAN) |
| 3 | Deepam 2.0 | 3 free LPG cylinders per year to women |
| 4 | Free bus travel ('Stree Shakti') | Zero-fare travel for women in state (APSRTC) buses |
| 5 | Adabidda Nidhi | ~₹1,500/month to eligible women aged 18–59 |
| 6 | Youth unemployment allowance ('Yuvashakti') | ~₹3,000/month to unemployed youth |

**Terms explained**
- **Thalliki Vandanam** — 'salute to the mother': schooling support paid to mothers per child.
- **Annadata Sukhibhava** — 'may the food-giver be happy': farmer income support that absorbs the central PM-KISAN amount.
- **Deepam 2.0** — free cooking-gas-cylinder scheme for women.
- **Adabidda Nidhi** — monthly cash support for women aged 18–59.

**Don't confuse**
- The **Super Six** (2024 TDP-NDA) are different from the earlier YSRCP package **Navaratnalu** (Amma Vodi, Rythu Bharosa, Aarogyasri, etc.) — the exam deliberately mixes the two.
- Amounts are approximate and some guarantees are being rolled out in **phases** through 2026, so treat figures as 'as announced'.

**Remember it**
Super Six = '**Mother, Farmer, Gas, Bus, Woman-cash, Youth-cash**'.

**TL;DR**
- AP 'Super Six' are the 2024 TDP-led NDA (TDP–JSP–BJP) government's flagship guarantees under CM Chandrababu Naidu.
- Thalliki Vandanam ≈ ₹15,000/year per child schooling support to mothers.
- Annadata Sukhibhava ≈ ₹20,000/year to farmer families, inclusive of central PM-KISAN.
- Deepam 2.0 = 3 free LPG cylinders/year; free bus travel = zero-fare for women in state buses.
- Adabidda Nidhi ≈ ₹1,500/month to women (18–59); youth get ≈ ₹3,000/month unemployment allowance.
- The previous YSRCP package 'Navaratnalu' (Amma Vodi, Rythu Bharosa) is a separate, older set.

items.title: Super Six — How They Interlock with Central Schemes
items.body:
### How the Super Six build on central schemes

**In one line**
Several Super Six guarantees are deliberately stacked on top of existing central schemes, so the state's rupee adds to — rather than duplicates — the Centre's, and most are paid by DBT.

**Why it is asked**
Questions test the convergence design (Annadata Sukhibhava includes PM-KISAN; Deepam complements Ujjwala) and the newer 'P4' poverty model.

**The story (cause → what happened → result)**
Running six guarantees is expensive, so the state designed them to **ride on central schemes** instead of paying twice. **Annadata Sukhibhava** counts the central **PM-KISAN ₹6,000** inside its ~₹20,000, with the state topping up the rest. **Deepam 2.0** pays for **free refills** on top of the central **Ujjwala** connection, so the connection (Centre) and the gas (State) work together. Delivery uses the same Aadhaar-linked DBT rails as central schemes.

**Picture it (state top-up on central base)**

| State guarantee | Central base it uses | What the state adds |
|---|---|---|
| Annadata Sukhibhava (~₹20,000) | PM-KISAN (₹6,000) | Top-up to reach ~₹20,000 |
| Deepam 2.0 (free refills) | Ujjwala (free connection) | Pays for the refills |

**Rollout, renamings and pensions (status 2026)**

| Scheme | When it started | Key detail | Replaced (YSRCP era) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Deepam-2 (free LPG) | 2024 — among the **first** Super Six promises implemented | 3 free cylinders a year | Deepam |
| Thalliki Vandanam | **12 June 2025** | ₹15,000 a year per school-going child, paid to the mother (not ₹25,000) | **Amma Vodi** |
| Annadata Sukhibhava–PM Kisan | **2 August 2025** | ₹20,000 a year = **₹14,000 State + ₹6,000 Centre** (PM-KISAN) | **YSR Rythu Bharosa** |
| Stree Shakti (free bus travel) | **15 August 2025** | Free travel for women in **non-AC RTC (public) buses** | — |
| NTR Bharosa Pensions | Enhanced from July 2024 | Old-age/widow pension raised from **₹3,000 to ₹4,000** a month; persons with disability **₹6,000** a month; higher amounts for the bedridden | **YSR Pension Kanuka** |

So NTR Bharosa is **tiered**, not a flat amount: ₹4,000 for old-age/widow pensioners, ₹6,000 for persons with disability.

**Swarna Andhra @2047.** The State's long-term vision, **launched in November 2024**, aims to make Andhra Pradesh a **developed state by 2047** (the centenary of Independence). It is built on **ten guiding principles called 'Padi Sutralu'** (zero poverty, employment, skilling, water security, energy, deep tech and others). Its **P4 (Public–Private–People Partnership)** model targets the **elimination of poverty**: better-off families ('Margadarsis') support the poorest ('Bangaru Kutumbalu'), aiming at zero poverty by 2029.

**Terms explained**
- **Convergence** — designing a state scheme so it adds to, instead of duplicating, a central scheme.
- **P4 (Public–Private–People Partnership)** — AP's poverty-reduction model pairing better-off families or private actors with the poorest households.
- **Mega DSC** — a large teacher-recruitment drive (District Selection Committee) promised alongside the guarantees.

**Don't confuse**
- Annadata Sukhibhava does **not** pay ₹20,000 on top of PM-KISAN — the ₹6,000 is **included** within it.
- 'P4' is a governance/poverty model, **not** one of the six cash guarantees.

**Remember it**
'**State tops up, Centre lays the base**' — Annadata on PM-KISAN, Deepam on Ujjwala.

**TL;DR**
- Annadata Sukhibhava is built on top of central PM-KISAN (₹6,000) with a state top-up to ~₹20,000.
- Deepam 2.0 (free refills) complements the central Ujjwala connection scheme.
- Super Six benefits are largely DBT-based via Aadhaar-linked accounts.
- AP's 'P4' = Public–Private–People Partnership model for poverty reduction.
- Allied promises included Mega DSC teacher recruitment and ration door-delivery.
keyPoints: Annadata Sukhibhava is built on top of central PM-KISAN (₹6,000) with a state top-up to ~₹20,000.
Deepam 2.0 (free refills) complements the central Ujjwala connection scheme.
Super Six benefits are largely DBT-based via Aadhaar-linked accounts.
AP's 'P4' = Public–Private–People Partnership model for poverty reduction.

Renamed: Amma Vodi → Thalliki Vandanam (12 Jun 2025); YSR Rythu Bharosa → Annadata Sukhibhava (2 Aug 2025, ₹14,000 State + ₹6,000 PM-KISAN); YSR Pension Kanuka → NTR Bharosa (₹4,000; disabled ₹6,000).
Stree Shakti (15 Aug 2025) = free non-AC RTC bus travel for women; Swarna Andhra @2047 (Nov 2024) rests on ten 'Padi Sutralu'.

items.title: Newer Central Schemes for Livelihoods & Energy
items.body:
### The newer livelihood and energy schemes

**In one line**
A recent wave of central schemes targets groups earlier schemes missed — street vendors, traditional artisans and rooftop-solar households.

**Why it is asked**
Being new, these are high-probability current-affairs items: the target group, launch year and headline number (18 trades, 1 crore homes, 300 units) are all testable.

**The story (cause → what happened → result)**
As older schemes covered farmers and the poorest, the Centre turned to the 'missing middle' of the informal economy. **PM SVANidhi** gave **street vendors** collateral-free working capital; **PM Vishwakarma (2023)** gave **traditional artisans** in 18 trades skilling, a toolkit and credit; and **PM Suryaghar Muft Bijli Yojana (2024)** pushed **rooftop solar** into ordinary homes to cut power bills.

**Picture it (scheme → group → headline)**

| Scheme | Target group | Headline |
|---|---|---|
| PM SVANidhi | Street vendors | Collateral-free micro-loans, digital-transaction incentives |
| PM Vishwakarma (2023) | Artisans (18 trades) | Skilling + toolkit + collateral-free credit |
| PM Suryaghar (2024) | Households | Rooftop solar, 1 crore homes, up to 300 free units/month |
| PMAY-Urban 2.0 (2024) | Urban poor | Additional urban houses sanctioned |
| PM MUDRA Yojana (2015) | Non-corporate small/micro enterprises | Collateral-free business loans (Shishu, Kishore, Tarun) through banks and NBFCs |

**Terms explained**
- **Collateral-free credit** — a loan given without the borrower pledging security/assets.
- **18 trades (PM Vishwakarma)** — traditional crafts such as carpenter, blacksmith, potter, cobbler, tailor and others.
- **Rooftop solar** — solar panels on a home's roof; the subsidy and up-to-300 free units cut the electricity bill.

**Don't confuse**
- **PM SVANidhi** (street vendors) vs **PM Vishwakarma** (traditional artisans and craftspeople) vs **PM MUDRA** (non-corporate small/micro enterprises) — three different informal groups.
- **PM Suryaghar** (rooftop solar for homes) is a **New & Renewable Energy** scheme, not a housing scheme.

**Remember it**
'**Vendor–Artisan–Solar**' = SVANidhi, Vishwakarma, Suryaghar — the new 'missing-middle' trio.

**TL;DR**
- PM SVANidhi gives collateral-free micro-loans to street vendors; PM Vishwakarma (2023) supports 18 traditional artisan trades.
- PM Suryaghar Muft Bijli Yojana (2024) targets 1 crore rooftop-solar homes, up to 300 free units/month.
- PMAY-Urban 2.0 was approved in 2024; PMAY-Gramin extended with more sanctioned houses.
- These newer schemes emphasise livelihoods, clean energy and the missing 'last-mile' groups.

items.title: Implementation, Convergence & Accountability
items.body:
### Why schemes succeed or fail on the ground

**In one line**
A good scheme can still fail in delivery, so this note covers the common implementation problems and the tools — DBT, social audit, outcome budgeting, 2nd ARC reforms — that fix them.

**Why it is asked**
Mains and prelims both ask about 'implementation gaps' and the accountability tools (social audit under MGNREGA, outcome budgeting, CPGRAMS).

**The story (cause → what happened → result)**
Money sanctioned at the top often does not reach the right person because beneficiary lists have **exclusion and inclusion errors**, funds **leak**, the **last mile** is understaffed, and overlapping schemes do not **converge**. In response, the government added **DBT + JAM** to plug leakages, **social audit** to let citizens check works, **outcome budgeting** to measure results rather than spending, and acted on **2nd ARC** recommendations for single-window, citizen-centric delivery.

**Picture it (problem → fix)**

| Problem | Fix |
|---|---|
| Leakage, ghost beneficiaries | DBT + JAM |
| Works not verified by citizens | Social audit (MGNREGA, Gram Sabha) |
| Spending measured, not results | Outcome budgeting |
| Grievances unresolved | CPGRAMS, single-window delivery |

**Terms explained**
- **Exclusion / inclusion error** — leaving out a genuine beneficiary, or wrongly including an ineligible one.
- **Social audit** — public scrutiny of a scheme's works by the Gram Sabha; it is statutorily mandated under **MGNREGA**.
- **Outcome budgeting** — a budget that tracks measurable outcomes (results), not just outlays (money spent).
- **2nd ARC** — the Second Administrative Reforms Commission, whose reports pushed citizen-centric, single-window governance.
- **P4 (Public–Private–People Partnership)** — the AP government's model aimed at poverty reduction, used alongside ward/village secretariats for last-mile delivery.
- **CPGRAMS** — the Centralised Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System.

**Don't confuse**
- **Outlay** (money allocated) vs **outcome** (result achieved) — outcome budgeting measures the second.
- Social audit is a **statutory** right under **MGNREGA**, not an optional review.

**Remember it**
'**Right list, no leak, real outcome, heard grievance**' — the four tests of good implementation.

**TL;DR**
- Key challenges: exclusion/inclusion errors, leakages, thin last-mile capacity, weak convergence, fiscal strain.
- Outcome budgeting shifts focus from outlays to measurable outcomes.
- Social audit is statutorily mandated under MGNREGA (Gram Sabha scrutiny).
- 2nd ARC pushed citizen-centric, single-window delivery and grievance redressal (CPGRAMS).
- AP relies on ward/village secretariats and the P4 model for last-mile delivery.

items.title: PYQ Precision — Scheme Numbers, Matching & YSR-era AP
items.body:
### Precision facts the exam tests on schemes

**In one line**
A quick-reference of the exact numbers (insurance cover, crop-premium rates), scheme-to-ministry matches and the YSR-era AP schemes that previous-year questions keep using.

**Why it is asked**
These are pure recall items where one wrong figure (premium rate, cover amount) or a swapped scheme name flips the answer.

**The story (why the traps work)**
Many schemes have similar acronyms (PMJJBY vs PMSBY) and the AP packages changed with the 2024 government, so examiners test whether you know the exact figure and the right era.

**Picture it — central-scheme facts**

| Scheme | Key number / fact |
|---|---|
| PMFBY (2016) | Farmer premium 2% Kharif / 1.5% Rabi / 5% commercial-horticulture |
| PMJJBY (2015) | Life insurance cover — ₹2 lakh |
| PMSBY (2015) | Accidental death/disability cover — ₹2 lakh |
| Atal Pension Yojana | Guaranteed pension in old age (unorganised sector) |
| Mission Indradhanush | Full immunisation of children and pregnant women |
| SWAYAM | Online MOOCs platform (Education Ministry) |
| DDU-GKY | Rural youth skilling and placement (MoRD) |
| MPLADS | Funds meant to create durable community assets; unused funds carried forward (do not lapse); the district authority is required to inspect a portion of the works (at least 10% each year) |

**YSR-era AP schemes (2019–24, 'Navaratnalu')**
- **Amma Vodi** — financial help to mothers for children's schooling (₹15,000/yr); **YSR Rythu Bharosa** — farmer income support (+PM-KISAN); **YSR Aarogyasri** — health insurance cover; **YSR Cheyutha** — women 45–60; **Jagananna Vidya Deevena** — fee reimbursement.
- These are distinct from the **2024 NDA 'Super Six'** (Thalliki Vandanam, Annadata Sukhibhava, Deepam-2, free bus travel, Adabidda Nidhi, youth allowance).

**Terms explained**
- **PMFBY** — Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana, the crop-insurance scheme; the farmer pays only 2%/1.5%/5% of the premium.
- **PMJJBY / PMSBY** — the ₹2-lakh life and accident micro-insurance schemes (both 2015).
- **MPLADS** — the MP Local Area Development Scheme; its funds do not lapse at year-end.
- **MOOCs** — Massive Open Online Courses, delivered via SWAYAM.

**Don't confuse**
- **PMJJBY = life** cover vs **PMSBY = accident** cover (both ₹2 lakh) — the exam swaps these.
- **Amma Vodi** (YSR 2019–24) vs **Thalliki Vandanam** (NDA 2024) — both pay mothers for schooling, but belong to different governments.

**Remember it**
'**JJ = Jeevan (life), SB = Suraksha (accident)**'; MPLADS funds **carry forward**.

**TL;DR**
- PMFBY farmer premium: 2% Kharif, 1.5% Rabi, 5% commercial/horticultural crops.
- PMJJBY = life cover, PMSBY = accident cover (each ₹2 lakh, 2015); Atal Pension Yojana = old-age pension.
- Mission Indradhanush = immunisation; SWAYAM = MOOCs; DDU-GKY = rural skilling.
- MPLADS funds build durable assets and can be carried forward (do not lapse).
- YSR-era AP schemes: Amma Vodi (schooling), Rythu Bharosa (farmers), Aarogyasri (health) — distinct from the 2024 Super Six.

items.title: Central Schemes in Full — Launch Dates, Benefits and the New Rural Jobs Law (October 2026)
items.body:
## The scheme calendar and the 2025 rural-jobs reform

**In one line:** most flagship schemes date from **2014-2019**, the **VB-G RAM G Act, 2025** has replaced **MGNREGA**, and a new wave (2023-25) targets tribal groups, pensions, farm districts and first jobs.

**Why it is asked:** launch years, launch places, benefit amounts and the MGNREGA replacement are the most likely scheme items in 2026-27.

**The story**

### Rural jobs: MGNREGA to VB-G RAM G
- **MGNREGA** (Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act) — passed **23 August 2005**, in force **February 2006**; **100 days** of guaranteed wage work.
- **Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, 2025 (VB-G RAM G)** — passed by Parliament in **December 2025**, assent **21 December 2025**, in force from **1 July 2026**; guarantees **125 days**; cost shared **60:40** by Centre and States (**90:10** for North-Eastern and Himalayan States); States may pause work for up to **60 days** in peak sowing and harvest seasons; **social audit** continues.

### Launch calendar
| Scheme | Launched | Key fact |
|---|---|---|
| **PMGSY** | **25 December 2000** | All-weather rural roads |
| **NFSA** | **2013** | Up to **75%** rural and **50%** urban population; **5 kg** grain per person a month; **35 kg** per AAY family |
| **PMGKAY** | 2020 | Free grain; extended for **five years** from **1 January 2024** |
| **PMJDY** | **28 August 2014** | Zero-balance accounts, RuPay card |
| **Swachh Bharat Mission** | **2 October 2014** | Open-defecation-free India |
| **Mission Indradhanush** | **25 December 2014** | Immunisation |
| **MUDRA** | **8 April 2015** | Shishu, Kishore, Tarun; **Tarun Plus** up to **₹20 lakh** (2024) |
| **PMJJBY, PMSBY, APY** | **9 May 2015**, Kolkata | Life ₹2 lakh, accident ₹2 lakh, pension |
| **Smart Cities Mission, AMRUT, PMAY-Urban** | **25 June 2015** | Smart Cities ended in **March 2025** |
| **Skill India** | **15 July 2015** | PMKVY training |
| **Stand-Up India** | **5 April 2016** | Loans of ₹10 lakh-₹1 crore to SC/ST and women entrepreneurs |
| **PM Ujjwala Yojana** | **1 May 2016**, **Ballia** | LPG connections for poor women |
| **PMAY-Gramin** | **20 November 2016** | Rural houses |
| **POSHAN Abhiyaan** | **8 March 2018**, **Jhunjhunu** | Nutrition |
| **PM-JAY** | **23 September 2018**, **Ranchi** | ₹5 lakh a family; **Ayushman Vay Vandana** card for all **70+** (October 2024) |
| **PM-KISAN** | **24 February 2019**, **Gorakhpur** | ₹6,000 a year |
| **Jal Jeevan Mission** | **15 August 2019** | Tap water; extended to **2028** |
| **PM SVANidhi** | **1 June 2020** | Street-vendor loans |
| **PM Vishwakarma** | **17 September 2023** | 18 artisan trades |
| **PM-JANMAN** | **15 November 2023** | **PVTGs** (particularly vulnerable tribal groups) |
| **PM Surya Ghar** | **13 February 2024** | **1 crore** rooftop-solar homes |
| **Unified Pension Scheme** | **1 April 2025** | **50%** of average basic pay for central staff with **25 years** of service |
| **PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana** | 2025 | **100** low-productivity farm districts |
| **PM Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana** | **1 August 2025** | Incentive for first jobs (about **3.5 crore** jobs) |

- The **Mid-Day Meal** scheme was renamed **PM POSHAN** in **September 2021**.

## Don't confuse
- **MGNREGA** (100 days) is replaced by **VB-G RAM G** (125 days) from 1 July 2026.
- **PM-JAY** began at **Ranchi**; **PM-KISAN** at **Gorakhpur**; **Ujjwala** at **Ballia**.

**TL;DR**
- VB-G RAM G Act 2025: 125 days, 60:40, 60-day farm-season pause, in force 1 July 2026.
- PMJDY 2014; Ujjwala 2016 Ballia; PM-JAY 2018 Ranchi; PM-KISAN 2019 Gorakhpur; JJM 2019.
- Newer: PM Vishwakarma 2023; PM-JANMAN 2023; Surya Ghar 2024; UPS 2025; PM-VBRY 2025.
keyPoints: The VB-G RAM G Act 2025 (assent 21 December 2025) replaced MGNREGA from 1 July 2026, guaranteeing 125 days with 60:40 Centre-State funding and a pause of up to 60 days in peak farm seasons.
MGNREGA was passed on 23 August 2005 and guaranteed 100 days; the NFSA 2013 covers up to 75% rural and 50% urban people with 5 kg grain a month.
Launch places: PM Ujjwala at Ballia (1 May 2016), POSHAN Abhiyaan at Jhunjhunu (8 March 2018), PM-JAY at Ranchi (23 September 2018), PM-KISAN at Gorakhpur (24 February 2019).
PMJJBY, PMSBY and Atal Pension Yojana were launched at Kolkata on 9 May 2015; MUDRA on 8 April 2015 (Tarun Plus up to ₹20 lakh); Stand-Up India on 5 April 2016.
PM-JANMAN (15 November 2023) is for PVTGs; PM Surya Ghar (13 February 2024) targets 1 crore homes; the Unified Pension Scheme began on 1 April 2025.
PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana covers 100 farm districts; PM Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana began on 1 August 2025; Mid-Day Meal became PM POSHAN in 2021.

items.title: Andhra Pradesh Schemes in Full — Status, Amounts and Launch Dates (October 2026)
items.body:
## Where AP's welfare promises stand

**In one line:** four of the **Super Six** are running (Deepam-2, Thalliki Vandanam, Annadata Sukhibhava, Stree Shakti), pensions have been raised, and new policies cover **health (₹25 lakh)**, **poverty (P4)**, **cheap meals** and **teacher recruitment**.

**Why it is asked:** APPSC sets state-scheme items on names, amounts, launch dates and which promise is still pending.

**The story**

### Super Six — status
| Scheme | Launch | Benefit |
|---|---|---|
| **Deepam-2** | **1 November 2024**, from **Srikakulam** district | **3** free LPG cylinders a year |
| **Thalliki Vandanam** | **12 June 2025** | **₹15,000** a year per school-going child; **₹13,000** is credited to the **mother** and **₹2,000** goes to the school maintenance fund; second-year payment from **22 July 2026** |
| **Annadata Sukhibhava–PM Kisan** | **2 August 2025** | **₹20,000** a year (₹14,000 State + ₹6,000 PM-KISAN); about **46.86 lakh** farmers |
| **Stree Shakti** | **15 August 2025** | Free travel for women in non-AC RTC buses |
| **Adabidda Nidhi** (₹1,500 a month to women) and **youth allowance** (₹3,000 a month) | Still **pending** in 2026 | Opposition protests in June 2026 over unfulfilled promises |

### Other schemes and policies
- **NTR Bharosa Pensions** — ₹4,000 a month (old age, widows), ₹6,000 (disability), up to ₹15,000 (bedridden); about **63 lakh** pensioners; **₹33,485 crore** in the **2026-27** budget.
- **P4 (Zero Poverty)** — launched at **Amaravati** on **Ugadi, 30 March 2025**; well-off "**Margadarsis**" adopt poor "**Bangaru Kutumbalu**".
- **Universal health policy** — approved by the Cabinet on **4 September 2025**; cover up to **₹25 lakh** for every family (about **5 crore** people).
- **Anna Canteens** — reopened on **15 August 2024**; a meal costs **₹5**.
- **Mega DSC 2025** — **16,347** teacher posts; **15,941** appointment orders by **September 2025**.
- **Matsyakarula Sevalo** — **₹20,000** per fishing family for the **61-day** fishing ban; **₹262 crore** to **1.30 lakh** families in **May 2026**.

## Don't confuse
- **Thalliki Vandanam** pays **₹13,000** to the mother of the ₹15,000 sanctioned; **Amma Vodi** was the earlier YSRCP scheme.
- **Deepam-2** began in **2024**, before the other Super Six; **Adabidda Nidhi** has not started.

**TL;DR**
- Deepam-2 1 November 2024; Thalliki Vandanam 12 June 2025 (₹13,000 + ₹2,000); Annadata 2 August 2025 (46.86 lakh farmers); Stree Shakti 15 August 2025.
- P4 30 March 2025; health ₹25 lakh (September 2025); Anna Canteens ₹5 (August 2024).
- Mega DSC 16,347 posts; fishermen ₹20,000; pensions ₹33,485 crore (2026-27).
keyPoints: Deepam-2 was launched on 1 November 2024 from Srikakulam district — the first Super Six scheme to start.
Under Thalliki Vandanam ₹13,000 of the ₹15,000 per child goes to the mother and ₹2,000 to the school maintenance fund; the second-year payment began on 22 July 2026.
Annadata Sukhibhava covers about 46.86 lakh farmers; Adabidda Nidhi and the youth allowance were still pending in 2026.
The P4 Zero Poverty programme was launched at Amaravati on Ugadi, 30 March 2025; the universal health policy (Cabinet, 4 September 2025) gives cover up to ₹25 lakh per family.
Anna Canteens reopened on 15 August 2024 with ₹5 meals; Mega DSC 2025 filled 16,347 teacher posts.
Matsyakarula Sevalo pays ₹20,000 per fishing family for the 61-day ban; NTR Bharosa pensions got ₹33,485 crore in 2026-27.

items.title: For Mains — Government Policies & Interventions for Development
items.body:
### For Mains — do welfare schemes deliver development?

**In one line**
For Mains (GS/Mains-3: policies and interventions for development, and the role of civil society/stakeholders), argue the trade-off between large welfare guarantees and fiscal sustainability, and how delivery design decides outcomes.

**The dimensions Mains asks**

| Dimension | What to write |
|---|---|
| Rationale | Constitutional DPSP goals; reducing poverty, hunger, exclusion |
| Design | Central Sector vs CSS; DBT + JAM; convergence to avoid duplication |
| Successes | Ujjwala, PMJDY financial inclusion, DBT leakage savings, Ayushman cover |
| Implementation gaps | Exclusion errors, last-mile capacity, weak convergence, data privacy |
| Freebie vs welfare debate | Fiscal strain on states (AP Super Six), opportunity cost vs capability-building |
| Stakeholders | Civil society, NGOs, SHGs, Gram Sabha social audit, private actors (AP's P4) |
| Way forward | Outcome budgeting, saturation approach, 2nd ARC single-window, strengthen Panchayats |

**Data points / reports to quote**
- DBT savings estimated at over ₹3 lakh crore cumulatively (Union government/NITI Aayog claims).
- JAM trinity and Aadhaar-linked transfers; PMJDY accounts in the tens of crores.
- MGNREGA (2005) social audit as a rights-based accountability model.
- 2nd ARC's citizen-centric administration reports; NITI Aayog Aspirational Districts Programme.
- AP's Super Six and 'P4' model as a current state-level case of the welfare-vs-fiscal debate.

**The AP angle**
Andhra's Super Six (Thalliki Vandanam, Annadata Sukhibhava, Deepam, free bus travel, Adabidda Nidhi, youth allowance) is a live example of welfare guarantees stretching state finances; the P4 model and ward/village secretariats show innovative last-mile delivery.

**Use in answers**
- Example: contrast DBT's leakage-plugging success with the fiscal risk of open-ended cash guarantees.
- Quote: welfare should build 'capability, not dependency' (Amartya Sen's capability approach).
- Diagram idea: a flow — Policy → Funding (CS/CSS) → DBT/JAM → Beneficiary → Social audit feedback.
keyPoints: Frame it as the welfare-vs-fiscal-sustainability trade-off, with delivery design deciding outcomes.
Cite DBT/JAM leakage savings, PMJDY inclusion, Ayushman cover as successes.
Implementation gaps: exclusion errors, last-mile capacity, weak convergence, data concerns.
Stakeholders: civil society, NGOs, SHGs, Gram Sabha social audit, AP's P4 private partnership.
AP angle: Super Six and P4 model as a current welfare-vs-fiscal case; way forward = outcome budgeting + saturation.
